title: Edge gateway signing rotation, SIEM ingest handover, and RBAC v2 audit mapping
content:
Purpose:
This note captures an operational playbook for rotating signing keys used by edge gateways (TLS and token signing), how rotation events are emitted into the RBAC v2 audit schema, and the downstream requirements for SIEM ingest and evidence automation so we maintain continuous compliance for private deployments.

Scope:
- Edge gateway components (ingress LB, API gateway, edge-auth service) deployed in customer VPCs (private deployments).
- mTLS and token signing keys (RSA/EC) used for service-to-service and client handshake verification.
- RBAC v2 audit events (authorization decisions, policy version, principal metadata).
- SIEM export: Elasticsearch (self-hosted customers) + Splunk + Azure Sentinel mapping.
- Evidence automation pipeline for audit evidence packages (daily snapshot + on-rotation delta).

High-level problem statement:
When gateway signing keys rotate, we must: (1) ensure zero-downtime rollout, (2) emit verifiable audit events that link rotation to operator identity and approval, (3) update SIEM ingest so historical and live logs can be correlated to the rotation window, and (4) produce an evidence package for compliance reviewers including signed manifests.

Edge architecture (text diagram):

  customer VPC subnet A                 customer VPC subnet B
  +-------------+                       +-------------+
  |  LB / ALB   |----> api-gateway ---> | edge-auth   |
  +-------------+                       +-------------+
           |                                      |
           |                                      +--> key-store (HSM/KMS)
           +---------------------------------------------> audit-producer (local)

Notes: key-store may be AWS KMS, GCP KMS, or an on-prem HSM depending on customer. The audit-producer is a small sidecar that signs and streams RBAC v2-compliant audit events to the local forwarding agent (fluentd/beat) which exports to SIEM.

Key rotation goals (operator acceptance criteria):
- No 5xx errors at the gateway for >99.9% during rotation window.
- All authorization decisions during rotation have a rotation_id field linking to rotation manifest.
- SIEM contains both rotation START and END events and can differentiate pre/post keys for traceability.
- Evidence package contains: rotation manifest, operator approval record, signer certificates, and verification script output.

Rotation workflow (recommended):
1) PREP: create rotation manifest in infra repo (PR), include: rotation_id, target_components, new_key_kid, expiry, rollback_plan, scheduled_window. PR must reference JIRA ticket.
2) APPROVAL: approval via SSO + GitHub PR (or manual sign-off in Support Console), recorded as operator_id and timestamp.
3) STAGE: deploy public cert/metadata for new key to a metadata endpoint (edge-metadata) so clients can fetch new KID without breaking existing sessions.
4) ZERO-DOWNTIME SWAP: enable dual-accept mode for 10 minutes where gateway accepts both old KID and new KID for token validation and signs with new key only (or signs with both if needed).
5) EMIT: audit-producer emits rotation.START event with rotation_id, operator_id, manifest hash, and target components.
6) MONITOR: watch metrics (5xx, latency, auth-deny) for the window; if thresholds exceed, trigger rollback.
7) FINALIZE: after stability window, emit rotation.END event; mark old key as deprecated in metadata and schedule deletion per retention policy.

RBAC v2 audit schema mapping (minimal required fields for rotation correlation):
- event_type: string ("rbac.authorization", "rotation.lifecycle")
- timestamp: RFC3339
- rotation_id: string (UUID)
- operator_id: string (SSO email / service account)
- actor_type: string (human | svc)
- action: string (e.g., "rotate-key", "approve-rotation", "finalize-rotation")
- resource: string ("gateway/edge-auth", "kms/key/abcd")
- decision: string (allow | deny | system)
- policy_version: string
- old_kid: string (nullable)
- new_kid: string (nullable)
- manifest_hash: string (sha256)
- evidence_refs: list (array of artifact URIs)  <-- represent as comma-separated string in logs if SIEM requires flat fields

Example audit event (as line-delimited JSON string to be sent by audit-producer):
{"event_type":"rotation.lifecycle","timestamp":"2025-01-18T15:24:11Z","rotation_id":"rot-9b1c4f","operator_id":"priya.shah@redwood.com","actor_type":"human","action":"rotate-key","resource":"gateway/edge-auth","decision":"system","policy_version":"rbac-v2-2024-11","old_kid":"kid-old-7a","new_kid":"kid-new-3c","manifest_hash":"sha256:abc123...","evidence_refs":"s3://evidence/rot-9b1c4f/manifest.json,s3://evidence/rot-9b1c4f/approval.log"}

SIEM ingest requirements and mapping notes:
- Field flattening: some SIEMs (Splunk) prefer nested JSON; others (legacy ELK pipelines) prefer flattened key=value. Ensure fluentd/logstash pipeline includes both a flattened set and the original JSON body.
- Timestamp parsing: all rotation events must include RFC3339 timestamps and an ingest rule that normalizes timezone to UTC.
- Rotation window correlation: pipeline should create an index/alias per rotation_id for faster queries (e.g., logs-rotation-rot-9b1c4f).
- Evidence tags: attach tags: rotation_id, operator_id, policy_version to all logs emitted by affected components during the window.

Sample Logstash filter (text snippet for reference):
# if rotation lifecycle event, set routing fields
if [event_type] == "rotation.lifecycle" {
  mutate { add_field => { "[@metadata][rotation_id]" => "%{rotation_id}" } }
  date { match => [ "timestamp", "ISO8601" ] }
}

SIEM query examples (ad-hoc):
- Elasticsearch (Lucene):
  rotation_id: "rot-9b1c4f" OR message:"rot-9b1c4f"
- Splunk SPL (find rotation window):
  index=main rotation_id="rot-9b1c4f" | stats count by host, event_type
- Azure Sentinel KQL (detect missing rotation.end within 24h):
  SecurityEvent
  | where EventTime >= ago(7d) and rotation_id != ""
  | summarize hasEnd = any_if(EventType == "rotation.lifecycle" and action=="finalize-rotation", 1, 0) by rotation_id
  | where hasEnd == 0

Firewall and VPC rules (practical examples):
- Principle: minimize admin plane access; TTL for admin IP allowlist; require mTLS + client cert subject check for admin endpoints.

AWS SG example (conceptual):
- sg-edge-admin: allow TCP 8443 from admin-bastion-cidr/32 (expiration tag: "2025-01-31T00:00:00Z")
- sg-edge-internal: allow TCP 443 from internal-subnet (service mesh)

iptables example for edge-host (accept only mTLS client certs):
# note: system-level mTLS enforcement happens in envoy/nginx config; iptables limits source IPs
iptables -A INPUT -p tcp --dport 8443 -s 10.0.0.0/16 -j ACCEPT
iptables -A INPUT -p tcp --dport 8443 -j DROP

mTLS recommendations for private deployments:
- Use mutual TLS with client certificate CN including tenant-id and service role.
- Gateway validates cert CN and OID for role binding, then maps to RBAC principal_id in audit event.
- Rotate client certs on a monthly cadence for short-lived non-prod, quarterly for prod, with emergency rotation process documented.

Evidence automation pipeline (daily snapshot + rotation delta):
1) Daily snapshot job collects: cluster config, active KIDs, active policies, recent audit index metadata.
2) On rotation.START: create a delta evidence container and start streaming audit logs + metrics for the rotation window into the container.
3) Post-finalize: run verification script that replays signature checks against saved keys, produce signed verification.log and include it in the evidence container.
4) Sign the entire evidence container manifest with operator SSO key (or cross-signed by Legal key for retention packages).
5) Upload to evidence bucket with retention metadata and generate an automated Jira ticket for compliance with links.

Verification scripts (checks to include):
- verify-manifest.sh: validates manifest hash vs stored manifest_hash in audit event.
- verify-signatures.py: attempts to verify tokens in sample request logs using both old and new KIDs where applicable and outputs pass/fail table.
- siem-ingest-check.sh: queries SIEM for presence of rotation.START and rotation.END events, flags missing items.

Operational playbook (short checklist):
- [ ] Create PR with rotation manifest and link JIRA ticket.
- [ ] Obtain 2 approvers from security and on-call owner.
- [ ] Stage metadata endpoint with new KID.
- [ ] Enable dual-accept on gateway; monitor 5xx and auth-deny rate.
- [ ] Emit rotation.START and verify SIEM receives it (use siem-ingest-check.sh).
- [ ] Finalize after stability window; emit rotation.END and run evidence pipeline.
- [ ] Upload signed evidence package; close JIRA ticket and tag PR as merged.

Rollbacks and incident notes:
- If auth-deny spikes >0.5% over baseline in 5m: automatically revert dual-accept config and re-enable old signing behaviors; emit rotation.FAIL with reason.
- Keep a 24h audit buffer: do not delete old keys for at least 24h after rotation.END unless explicitly approved by compliance.

Open items / TODOs:
- Add standard RBAC v2 field set to fluentd forwarder -> ensure parity across cloud providers. (owner: Daniel)
- Create a lightweight UI view in Console showing rotation status per customer (owner: Marcus)
- Add prebuilt KQL and Splunk dashboards to infra repo for rotation evidence queries (owner: Eva)

References and links:
- Confluence RBAC v2 spec: https://confluence.redwood.com/display/INF/RBAC+v2+Schema
- Infra PR w/ dual-accept gateway code: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/1012
- JIRA template: JIRA-1258 (rotation workflow template)

Contact and escalation:
- On-call: eng-private-deployments paging policy (Slack #eng-pd-oncall, escalation to SRE lead)
- Security review: security-team@redwood.com

Notes to self / rough ideas:
- Could attach a small signed timeline (tz-aware) to evidence package that lists all operator actions (almost like a blockchain-lite).
- Consider exposing rotation metadata via a customer-visible endpoint so customers can independently verify key state.

End of draft.
